pairs.subject: engine-host-contract
pairs.evidence: crates/runner/Cargo.toml:6 lt-runner embeds no language engine: its dependency block has core, render, billing, anon, serde, chrono, clap, reqwest, anyhow and dotenvy, and `lighttrack-engine` is the LLM-judge driver, not an interpreter. I searched the runner sources and the whole repo (*.rs, *.toml) for boa_engine, quickjs, deno_core, rhai, mlua, wasmtime, JobExecutor, HostHooks, ModuleLoader, microtask, interpreter and guest and found nothing, so there are no host hooks, job executors, guest module loader or engine clock seam for this subject to govern.

techniques.evidence: crates/runner/src/dispatch.rs:1 Dispatch maps durable JobKind records to handlers. There is no specification-defined host-hook table to mirror.

crates/runner/src/serve.rs:111 The serve loop polls a leased job queue over HTTP (the job-coordination subject, which the golden path explicitly excludes). It does not drain microtask or macrotask queues for an engine.
crates/runner/src/serve.rs:77 Jobs are claimed from the API with leases. No engine ships a null or blocking promise executor.
crates/runner/src/labels.rs:99 The runner only reads files the operator names on the CLI. No guest import specifiers are resolved.
crates/runner/src/serve.rs:18 Timing here is the host's own lease heartbeat. No guest timers or dates are exposed through a clock seam.
crates/runner/Cargo.toml:16 The only 'engine' dependency is the LLM-judge crate. There is no traced guest heap whose jobs could need to be roots.
